batch_strategy: Freeze these 32 IDs and their supplied packet V1/V2 predictions together. Prioritize interpretable experiments around newly exposed endpoint-specific failures, loading contrasts, and solvent-response transitions. Extend those tests to related ether and carbonyl environments where transfer remains uncertain. Use the single predictor's quantile widths as secondary evidence, without treating them as calibrated epistemic uncertainty.

choices.reason: m177 at 50/1, 50 ul tests whether the compact low-loading exception persists at weaker solvent. Measured 20/1 completion is 8.50 mL at 50 ul (aa43fe84c0d8c825fe58), versus 57.02 mL at 150 ul (5e276c1730fc0a9deba7). The current 50/1 forecast is already 7.85/74.83 mL; this label can distinguish transfer of the long interval from a loading-specific response.

m177 at 50/1, 100 ul supplies the middle amount between the selected 50-ul experiment and measured 150-ul b514312eda7950cdcf1c, which gave 4.49/81.30 mL. The two candidate forecasts are nearly identical despite their different amounts. This contrast can teach an amount interaction or show that the earlier compact observation is localized elsewhere.

m177 at 10/1, 50 ul places a solvent-only extension before measured 20/1 at the same loading (aa43fe84c0d8c825fe58). Its predicted completion, 25.38 mL, exceeds that measured 20/1 completion of 8.50 mL. Together with the selected higher-loading 10/1 point, it tests whether this apparent reversal is a recorded response or a consequence of blending conflicting anchors.

m177 at 10/1, 150 ul completes a fixed-loading 10/20/50 curve with 5e276c1730fc0a9deba7 and b514312eda7950cdcf1c. The forecast is 4.77/25.39 mL. Measuring it locates the emergence of long completion while testing whether onset remains early, independently of the selected 50-ul curve.

m75 at 10/1, 50 ul extends measured 5/1 at the same loading (c641cb5b9e82e60de614) and helps interpret the unexpectedly early 50/1 result 28e9fea3e3293f2b8a0e. The paired 150-ul experiment asks whether the large boundary amount contrast is already visible at this intermediate ratio.

m75 at 10/1, 150 ul tests the model's nearly unchanged forecast across the selected amounts, approximately 10.82/23.22 mL. Measured 50/1 at 150 ul was 37.94/51.52 mL (9249ed2c527f70995033), far later than the 50-ul boundary. This label separates an amount effect confined to weak solvent from one beginning earlier in the response.

m212 at 5/1, 100 ul fills the amount gap between measured 50-ul d5234e966aa231be05e5, 7.24/13.67 mL, and 150-ul 89d752b5a7f7c8d0b91e, 23.21/39.84 mL. The intermediate label can distinguish a gradual loading association from a sharper conditional change or variability at the extremes.

m212 at 10/1, 100 ul forms a solvent-only pair with the selected 5/1 point and an amount contrast with measured 150-ul 942b8fc9cf013acda52b. Its forecast is 35.61/54.68 mL. This tests how the secondary-amine response changes after the region where the latest low-loading label was substantially overpredicted.

m194 at 2/1, 150 ul completes an amount series around measured 50-ul 2bd4f8787a951ef0ee04 and 100-ul 66c6a533f485d5277f2f. Their completion volumes differ markedly, 14.73 versus 28.27 mL, while onset remains early. The current 150-ul forecast of 5.44/17.58 mL tests whether completion follows a nonlinear amount relationship.

m194 at 5/1, 50 ul extends the newly measured 1/1 and 2/1 low-loading curve (c0094343ab6bb16bc58b, 2bd4f8787a951ef0ee04) and contrasts with measured 5/1 at 100 ul (39815ababe97d7acc107). It tests whether the smaller low-loading completion interval persists as solvent weakens.

m108 at 50/1, 100 ul extends measured 20/1 at identical loading and plug conditions (941f69aeb5995f34ea50). The forecast remains near 8.02/16.99 mL. Paired with the positional isomer m122, it tests a predicted weak-solvent plateau in a bromodimethoxy environment after recent ether-transfer overpredictions.

m122 at 50/1, 100 ul is predicted at 20.14/35.91 mL, substantially later than the selected m108 isomer. Measured m122 anchors include 10/1 at 100 ul (cea0d1e24499911eed47) and 20/1 at 50 ul (27427ea5fe0b9eafb94a). This tests positional-environment transfer while retaining the isomers' different density-derived sample amounts.

m110 at 10/1, 100 ul supplies the first intermediate point between measured 0/1 ac52c50de335acae588d and 50/1 ce39d1762993bbbafaca at identical loading. The latter was much earlier than its acquisition forecast. This label tests where trimethoxybenzene begins its retention increase after that correction.

m110 at 20/1, 100 ul completes the selected fixed-loading intermediate pair. Its forecast, 19.47/31.46 mL, is already near measured 50/1 at 22.94/36.12 mL (ce39d1762993bbbafaca). Measuring both intermediates distinguishes an early rise followed by leveling from a differently placed transition.

m198 at 10/1, 100 ul fills the decisive gap between measured 5/1, 6.93/23.01 mL (4da6e3b93f29af1efa94), and 20/1, 24.17/56.91 mL (163874b97308a1ea2507). The current forecast is 12.32/27.25 mL. This tests transition placement after the latest weak-solvent underestimates.

m198 at 20/1, 50 ul supplies a clean amount contrast to measured 100-ul 163874b97308a1ea2507 with the same DCM plug. It asks whether the large loading-associated completion contrast seen for m177 extends to this ortho-nitroaldehyde or is localized to the benzophenone environment.

m159 at 10/1, 150 ul contrasts directly with newly measured 50-ul 58394a71418a9623e18a, 6.55/27.99 mL. The forecast remains similar at 6.93/26.54 mL despite the amount change. This tests amount sensitivity before the strong onset growth measured at 20/1 and 50/1 at 100 ul (a738b1f204da6fcfd385, a17bcdddcf0799baeee2).

m95 at 5/1, 50 ul explores an unmeasured part of the methyl beta-ketoester response. Its predicted completion of 38.60 mL exceeds the selected 10/1 forecast. Measured 10/1 and 20/1 at 150 ul (35944fdd59ac331c3fcb, d448d8de2d8dacec62c3) provide context, but do not resolve this lower-loading curve.

m95 at 10/1, 50 ul completes the selected solvent-only pair and contrasts with measured 150-ul 35944fdd59ac331c3fcb. Measuring both points tests the predicted 5-to-10/1 completion plateau or reversal and separates solvent response from amount dependence within a common beta-ketoester motif.

m164 at 1/1, 100 ul tests a new strong-solvent anomaly: predicted 11.01/26.39 mL versus 6.86/13.16 mL for the selected 2/1 point. Measured 0/1 and 5/1 are comparatively early (5df546d9e2f2a29dfc89, 9f450a70d44f4384353f). The pair can identify which side of the forecast reversal needs correction.

m164 at 2/1, 100 ul supplies the other side of the predicted reversal at fixed sample amount and DCM plug. Together with measured 5/1 9f450a70d44f4384353f and the selected 1/1 point, it discriminates a localized recorded response from a misplaced strong-solvent prediction.

m73 at 0/1, 100 ul brackets the delayed-onset 1/1 record 2cf789c87f7c6325c020 and early 2/1 result 49932dbd3d16bb64f71a. The delayed 1/1 onset also appeared at 50 ul (a387411cbcb6be48bde4), although that record has V2 slightly below V1. This label constrains the localized recorded pattern without assigning it a physical mechanism.

m107 at 1/1, 100 ul adds a strong-solvent anchor at the same loading as measured 5/1 d1172a49fca1e196a59f, 35.16/96.51 mL. Measured 2/1 at 150 ul is already 14.15/42.35 mL (769f1d04efb22c05cfdf). The new label helps locate the early transition while retaining the amount difference at 2/1.

m107 at 5/1, 50 ul completes an amount series with measured 100-ul d1172a49fca1e196a59f and 150-ul 2cfa393cb79664e100ce. Both measured completions are long and fairly similar. This tests whether substantial loading effects found elsewhere should transfer to this ether-containing beta-ketoester.

m202 at 5/1, 50 ul supplies an intermediate anchor at the same amount as measured 2/1 c6e28d5262ab7fb32107 and the selected 10/1 point. Measured 5/1 at 100 ul is early (86258f5c8ffdb874521f). This establishes a controlled local response for the recorded phosphorus/oxygen scaffold.

m202 at 10/1, 50 ul forms the delayed side of the selected 5/10 pair. Measured 10/1 at 100 ul is 35.08/70.35 mL (902937db42f82f467718), whereas measured 5/1 at 100 ul is 6.82/13.06 mL (86258f5c8ffdb874521f). The pair tests whether that sharp conditional response transfers across amounts.

m191 at 5/1, 150 ul extends measured 2/1 at identical loading (53becf1a41d72abcc45a), whose endpoints were 7.07/23.74 mL. Measured 10/1 at 100 ul is much later (bae9d67e095423d8edd2). This tests where the dialdehyde transition begins, with the remaining amount difference at 10/1 kept explicit.

m28 at 5/1, 150 ul fills a fully matched curve between measured 2/1 b05a4e8db42ce35cc958, 6.15/26.80 mL, and 10/1 0dccaa29989ef4956786, 38.78/80.88 mL. This label can locate the steep transition for an acetoxy-substituted aldehyde and improve transfer among aromatic compounds with multiple oxygen acceptors.

m195 at 50/1, 150 ul tests extension beyond the unusual high-loading 20/1 record a917c928912c74862968. That record has V2 below V1 and cannot establish a physical interval; coherent 100-ul 20/1 measurement 783cf2454912fc14bb80 has much earlier onset. A new solvent regime helps constrain how this conflicting anchor should influence prediction.

m8 at 50/1, 50 ul extends measured 20/1 at identical loading and plug conditions (6a4be1a58bc5ec9ed008). The forecast rises from that measured 6.04/13.79 mL to 15.42/27.53 mL. This tests weak-solvent transfer to a fused aromatic ether with a different acceptor environment from the methoxyarenes.

m6 at 20/1, 150 ul supplies an intermediate point between measured 1/1 at the same loading (93f069afca83e51f108f) and the selected 50/1 experiment. It explores the cyclic OCO arrangement through a controlled response curve, allowing comparison with the selected bromodimethoxy isomers without assuming equal behavior from HBA count.

m6 at 50/1, 150 ul completes the selected fixed-loading extension from 93f069afca83e51f108f. Its predicted 26.25/41.93 mL is substantially later than the selected m108 forecast, although their sample amounts differ. The two-point m6 curve tests whether this topology-dependent transfer is supported by labels.

hypotheses.content: Nitro-carbonyl response must be learned separately for onset, completion, and loading regime. The compact m177 20/1 observation at 50 ul does not transfer to 150 ul: the latter retains early onset but has very late completion. Whether low-loading compact behavior persists at other ratios, and whether this amount association extends to m198, remain unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest severe errors were predominantly in V2 for m177 but affected both endpoints for m198. Learning these distinctions can prevent a common nitro-family correction from obscuring endpoint and condition interactions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 50/1, how do m177 completion volumes vary across 50, 100, and 150 ul, and do the matched 10/1 labels show that the loading contrast begins before 20/1?

hypotheses.content: Recorded loading associations are scaffold- and solvent-dependent, with different effects on V1 and V2. The m75, m212, and m194 contrasts support meaningful local amount sensitivity, while the much smaller m119 contrast limits any universal large-loading correction. These observations do not establish a causal amount law or exclude experimental variability.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Several supplied forecasts change little across amounts despite large measured contrasts. Intermediate amounts and matched ratio pairs can teach interactions involving the density-times-volume feature while also identifying regions where amount effects are modest.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the m75 intermediate-ratio pair, m212 middle-amount curve, m194 amount extension, and m107 low-loading label support distinct local relationships rather than one shared amount correction?

hypotheses.content: Ether substitution environment and acceptor arrangement influence weak-solvent response beyond ether count alone. Recent m123 and m110 boundary labels weakened direct transfer from delayed m116. The predicted differences among bromodimethoxy isomers, cyclic OCO substitution, and fused aromatic ethers now need measurement. Across-molecule comparisons retain differences in loading amount and plug conditions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Related ether motifs appear across many rows. Local solvent-response labels can improve structural transfer and constrain where a correction learned from one arene should weaken, persist, or change shape.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m108 and m122 retain their predicted boundary difference, and do the m110 and m6 intermediate curves and m8 extension support the model's placement of their weak-solvent transitions?

hypotheses.content: The placement and endpoint shape of solvent-response transitions depend on acceptor context. Aromatic nitroaldehydes, substituted benzophenones, acetoxy aldehydes, and beta-ketoesters need not share an onset threshold or a common relationship between onset growth and completion growth. Current intermediate forecasts remain testable even where boundary predictions have already improved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Intermediate labels discriminate transition placement from endpoint offsets. This should improve interpolation across common carbonyl-containing rows and reduce both excessive transfer of delayed retention and missed completion growth.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do the selected m198, m159, m28, m191, m95, and m107 points place their transitions, and which responses change when sample amount is held fixed?

hypotheses.content: The current m164 prediction of substantially later onset and completion at 1/1 than at 2/1 may indicate a localized model failure or an unusual recorded conditional response. This reversal is presently a prediction, not an experimental finding.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A fixed-loading pair can identify a strong-solvent failure that acquisition focused on delayed boundaries would miss. Its outcome can constrain local behavior without imposing monotonicity on all recorded rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do measured m164 endpoints confirm the predicted 1/1-to-2/1 reversal, or does one side return to the early strong-solvent regime?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes substantially changed the priorities. For m177 at 150 ul, measured 20/1 and 50/1 endpoints were 4.78/57.02 and 4.49/81.30 mL; acquisition forecasts underestimated V2 by 45.75 and 66.14 mL while onset was close. This rejects persistence of the compact response at higher loading, while leaving the low-loading exception unresolved. Current 50/1 forecasts already reflect much longer completion, so the next useful tests concern amounts and transition placement. The m198 outcomes exposed delayed onset as well as completion; an intermediate 10/1 label now complements those repaired boundaries. The m75 boundary contrast, m212 5/1 amount contrast, and m194 completion contrast strengthened the case for local loading interactions, but the modest m119 amount change weakens a universal large-loading effect. Ether results also rejected broad upward transfer: m123 and m110 finished substantially earlier than their acquisition forecasts, whereas m116 remained more delayed. Their current predictions have changed, so I target new response relationships rather than assume historical errors persist. The m45 strong-solvent completion reversal and m156 endpoint anomaly were not confirmed. Delayed m73 onset at 1/1 appeared at another amount, but one record has V2 slightly below V1, so it supports a localized recorded pattern rather than a defensible physical interval mechanism.
batch_rationale: The batch uses the latest failures to identify relationships that remain unresolved after retraining. The m177 amount series and matched 10/1 pair distinguish a compact low-loading exception from broadly early onset with long completion. The m75, m212, m194, and m107 experiments test whether amount sensitivity begins at particular solvent regimes, differs between endpoints, or remains modest on another scaffold. Ether experiments probe transfer across substitution patterns after the recent m123 and m110 overpredictions; the m6 curve and m8 extension add targeted structural coverage with interpretable same-molecule contrasts. Carbonyl intermediates locate transitions between measured early and delayed regimes, while the m202 pair tests a sharp response in a different recorded heteroatom environment. Strong-solvent m164 and m73 measurements provide complementary information about localized forecast anomalies and conflicting anchors. Selected tuples are distinct within the batch. Ordinary regions with several coherent anchors and small recent errors receive less attention because their marginal learning value appears lower. These labels may improve overall Row accuracy by teaching shared structure-condition relationships while preserving measured exceptions. Elution-interval width is treated as a response property, and unexplained contrasts remain subject to experimental variability and missing metadata.
